title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to the notes for Grothendieck's 1976 IHES lecture on the divided-power (pd) de Rham complex. The heading announces a study of automorphisms of the 'affine simplicial (or 1/2-simplicial) ring' A_•. The NB says these automorphisms are no longer required to respect the S-algebra structure, S = A_0, i.e. they need not induce the identity on A_0.

The basic object. Let S be a commutative ring, S^+ ⊂ S an ideal with divided powers, and t ∈ S^+. Define
 A_n(S,S^+,t) = S{X_0,…,X_n}[dX_0,…,dX_n] / (ΣX_i − t, ΣdX_i)_pd.
Here:
- S{X} is the divided-power polynomial algebra.
- [dX] is the exterior algebra on the dX_i, so A_n is Λ-graded (graded by form degree).
- The quotient is by the pd-ideal generated by ΣX_i − t and ΣdX_i. This ideal makes sense because ΣX_i − t lies in the pd-ideal S^+ + (X_i)^{[≥1]}; this is exactly where t ∈ S^+ is used.

In modern terms, A_n is the algebra of pd-polynomial differential forms on the 'scaled pd-simplex' {ΣX_i = t}. It is an integral, divided-power analogue of Sullivan's polynomial de Rham forms ∇(n,•) on the simplex Σx_i = 1, with 1 replaced by a parameter t lying in the pd-ideal. As n varies, the usual coface/codegeneracy formulas (X_j ↦ 0, X_i ↦ X_i + X_{i+1}) preserve the relations ΣX_i = t and ΣdX_i = 0. So one gets a simplicial S-algebra, Λ-graded with pd; 'à 1/2 simplicial' presumably means only part of the structure is used.

Functoriality. Take a pd-morphism u: S → S' with u(S^+) ⊂ S'^+, a target triple (S', S'^+, t'), and λ ∈ S' with u(t) = λ t'. Then
 A_•(u,λ): A_•(S,S^+,t) → A_•(S',S'^+,t')
is given by u on scalars, X_i ↦ λX_i (hence X_i^{[k]} ↦ λ^k X_i^{[k]}), and dX_i ↦ λ dX_i. It is well defined because ΣX_i − t ↦ λΣX_i − u(t) = λ(ΣX_i − t'), and ΣdX_i ↦ λΣdX_i.

So A_• is a covariant functor on the category of triples (S,S^+,t), with morphisms the pairs (u,λ) and composition (u',λ')∘(u,λ) = (u'u, u'(λ)λ'). Check: X ↦ λX ↦ u'(λ)λ'X, and u'u(t) = u'(λ)u'(t') = u'(λ)λ' t''. The automorphisms of A_• over a fixed triple therefore include the 'rescalings' by λ with λ t = t. When t = 0, every λ ∈ S works, giving a G_m-type action; this is presumably what the heading is after.

Filtration. A_n carries a natural increasing filtration by total degree, with X_i and dX_i both of weight 1. Fil^m consists of the sums Σ F_{i_0…i_p} dX_{i_0}∧…∧dX_{i_p} with F of degree ≤ m − p. These are S-submodules but not ideals, with:
- Fil^m · Fil^{m'} ⊂ Fil^{m+m'};
- Fil^0 = S (the scalars);
- Fil^m = 0 for m < 0.
It is only a filtration, not a grading, because the relation ΣX_i − t is inhomogeneous. The maps A_•(u,λ) respect it, since they multiply each weight-1 generator by λ.

Purpose. The page is preparing the functorial (in (S,S^+,t)) pd-simplicial de Rham algebra and its symmetries, to be used for constructing pd de Rham–type functors. Comparing degree t = 1 (an honest simplex) with t ∈ S^+ (an infinitesimally scaled pd-simplex) and with t = 0 (a cone with a G_m-action) is implicit.
errors: Target written A'_•(S,S'^+,t'); it should be A_•(S',S'^+,t').
The scalar is introduced as λ' ∈ S' but used as λ in u(t) = λt'. Minor notational slip.
The index n is used both for the simplicial degree and for the filtration index (Fil^n A_n). This is a notation clash, not a mathematical error.
The formula 'Σ X_0 − t ↦ Σ λX_0 − …' should read Σ X_i; the substitution is meant for all X_i, not only X_0.

ideas.what: Simplicial algebra of divided-power polynomial differential forms on the simplex ΣX_i = t, with t in a pd-ideal
ideas.modern_name: Integral/pd analogue of Sullivan's polynomial de Rham forms (pd-simplicial de Rham algebra)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977) for rational polynomial forms; integral/divided-power variants by Cenkl–Porter (c. 1980s) and others (unsure of exact credits)

ideas.what: Functoriality in triples (S,S^+,t) with morphisms (u,λ), u(t) = λt', acting by X_i ↦ λX_i, dX_i ↦ λdX_i; composition law (u'u, u'(λ)λ')
ideas.modern_name: Rescaling / G_m-equivariance of the scaled simplex (deformation-to-the-cone type structure)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unclear; similar rescaling structures appear in filtered de Rham / deformation to the normal cone constructions

ideas.what: Increasing multiplicative filtration by polynomial-plus-form degree, Fil^0 = S, preserved by the rescalings

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to study automorphisms of the pd-simplicial de Rham algebra that are not S-linear, i.e. rescalings X ↦ λX of the simplex ΣX_i = t with t in a pd-ideal. This gives a family interpolating between the simplex and the cone (t = 0) with a G_m-type symmetry. An integral pd version of simplicial polynomial forms, parametrized by t in a pd-ideal and functorial in (u,λ), does not seem to be standard in the literature.
missed.quote: Automorphismes de l'anneau affine simplicial à 1/2 simplicial A_• (NB. on ne demande plus de respecter la structure de S algèbre, S = A_0)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral models of rational/pd homotopy theory and filtered de Rham constructions with G_m-actions are active topics (e.g. integral de Rham models, filtered/Hodge deformations). An early pd-simplicial construction with a rescaling parameter could be of historical interest, but the page itself only sets up definitions.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, early (1976) setup of divided-power polynomial forms on scaled simplices with a parameter t in a pd-ideal and rescaling functoriality. That predates or parallels integral polynomial-form work and is not in Grothendieck's published texts. However, the page itself contains only definitions and routine verifications.
transcription_corrections: 'construire diverses foncteurs [?]' – likely 'pour construire diverses fonctions/foncteurs qui à un anneau comm. S …' (associating to a ring S …).
'le tout des sous-S-modules (pas pas des idéaux)' – read '(mais pas des idéaux)'.
S{X_0,…,X_n} denotes the divided-power polynomial algebra; the subscript 'pd' on the ideal denotes the pd-ideal generated.
